known.title: The plan pins Bun 1.4.4 only in `engines.bun` and keeps `packageManager` at `bun@1.4.0`, but setup-bun reads `packageManager` first, so CI keeps Bun 1.4.0.
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 7 (line 81); Steps, row 2 author_tooling_on_bun, Task cell (line 120); Research, Sources, setup-bun bullet (line 109)
known.summary: Decision 7 keeps `packageManager` at `bun@1.4.0` and pins the runtime only in a new `package.json` field `engines.bun` = `1.4.4`, because it says that setup-bun reads `engines.bun` first when the workflow gives no `bun-version`. Step 2 makes only this change. The setup-bun v2.2.0 README (https://github.com/oven-sh/setup-bun/blob/v2.2.0/README.md, section Usage) gives the opposite order: if no version is specified, the action will "1. Check `package.json` for the `packageManager` field" and "2. If `packageManager` doesn't exist, check `package.json` for `engines.bun`". The source at that tag (src/utils.ts line 124) returns `pkg.packageManager?.split("bun@")?.[1] ?? pkg.engines?.bun`. At repo_ref, `package.json:4` is `"packageManager": "bun@1.4.0"`, and each setup-bun step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:109`, `:175`, `:241`, `.github/workflows/dependency-integrity.yml:25`) uses `oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0` with no `with:` input. Effect: CI continues to install Bun 1.4.0, while the plan measures on 1.4.4 and says that the gate depends on the `node:child_process` fixes of Bun 1.4.3 (https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.3: `spawnSync` or `execFileSync` "could spin at 100% CPU and never return", which users hit "in large `bun test --isolate` suites"; `bun test --parallel` implies `--isolate`, https://bun.com/docs/test/parallel). Correct approach: change `packageManager` to `bun@1.4.4`, or give each setup-bun step an explicit `bun-version`.

known.title: The plan says that `bun test --timeout` takes seconds and sets `--timeout=180`, but Bun reads the value in milliseconds, so each unit test gets 180 ms.
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 5 (line 79); Steps, row 1 runtime_neutral_tests, Done when cell (line 119); Steps, row 2 author_tooling_on_bun, Task cell (line 120)
known.summary: Decision 5 says that `bun test --timeout` takes seconds and sets 180 for the longest child timeout (180 s). Step 1 Done when and the step 2 `test:unit` script both use `bun test --parallel=4 --timeout=180 ./scripts/tests/unit/*.test.mjs`. The Bun test runner documentation (https://bun.com/docs/test, section Timeouts) says: "Use the `--timeout` flag to specify a _per-test_ timeout in milliseconds. If a test times out, Bun marks it as failed. The default value is `5000`." So `--timeout=180` gives each test 180 ms, which is less than the 5000 ms default. At repo_ref, `scripts/tests/unit/agent-score-vacuity.test.mjs:96-99` and `scripts/tests/unit/skill-score-vacuity.test.mjs:81-84` run a full plugin gate in each test with `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['scripts/ci.mjs', '--plugin', TARGET], { ..., timeout: 180_000 })` (the Node `spawnSync` timeout is in milliseconds). A local probe with Bun 1.4.4 shows that `bun test --timeout=180` kills a `spawnSync` child that runs for 1 s and fails the test with "this test timed out after 180ms". Effect: these tests fail under the new `test:unit`, so step 1 and step 2 cannot reach their Done when, and the `bun run test:unit` call of the gate (`scripts/ci.mjs:302`) fails. The correct flag for 180 s is `--timeout=180000`.

known.title: Step 2 changes the gate run lines in ci.yml to `bun scripts/ci.mjs`, but no step updates `scripts/lib/ci-targeting.mjs`, whose parser matches only `node scripts/ci.mjs`.
known.locator: Steps, row 2 author_tooling_on_bun, Task and Files cells (line 120); Research, Decisions, decision 8 (line 82)
known.summary: Decision 8 and step 2 change the run lines of the `run the authoritative gate (scripts/ci.mjs)` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (lines 295, 296, and 298 at repo_ref) from `node scripts/ci.mjs` to `bun scripts/ci.mjs`. No step updates the parser that reads these lines: no Files cell names `scripts/lib/ci-targeting.mjs`, and no Task names it (`plan-contract.md:70-71` at repo_ref: `Files` defines the scope of a step). At repo_ref, `extractCiGateInvocations()` (`scripts/lib/ci-targeting.mjs:402-451`) keeps only the lines that match `/^(.*?)node\s+scripts\/ci\.mjs\b(.*)$/` (line 427), and it throws "run the authoritative gate (scripts/ci.mjs) never invokes scripts/ci.mjs" when it finds none (line 449). `scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs:2327` calls `assertAuthoritativeGateCoversReleasedBytes(authoritativeGateRun)` at module scope on the run body of that step, and this function calls the parser (`scripts/lib/ci-targeting.mjs:454`). After step 2, the parser finds no invocation and throws, so `bun scripts/tests/ci-plugin-targeting.mjs` fails: the step 2 Done when, Acceptance a3, and the `targeting-contracts` CI job cannot pass. Correct approach: add `scripts/lib/ci-targeting.mjs` to step 2 and make the parser match `bun scripts/ci.mjs`.

known.title: Acceptance a4 expects only exit 0 with 72 pass and 0 fail from `bun run test:unit`, which the unchanged Node `test:unit` script already gives.
known.summary: A4 runs `bun run test:unit` and expects "exits 0 and reports 72 pass, 0 fail". This row passes on the unchanged repository. At repo_ref, `package.json:13` defines `test:unit` as `node --test --test-concurrency=4 scripts/tests/unit/*.test.mjs`, and `scripts/ci.mjs:302` already runs `bun run test:unit` in the gate. `bun run` does not replace `node` in a package script unless `--bun` or `bunfig.toml` `[run] bun = true` is set (https://bun.com/docs/runtime: "By default, Bun respects this shebang and executes the script with `node`. The `--bun` flag overrides it"; https://bun.com/docs/runtime/bunfig, `run.bun`: "When `true`, Bun prepends `$PATH` with a `node` symlink that points to the `bun` binary"). `bunfig.toml` at repo_ref has only an `[install]` section. The 7 unit files at repo_ref hold 72 `test(` calls (7, 6, 25, 13, 8, 4, and 9), and the plan's Measurements table gives 72 pass for `node --test --test-concurrency=4`. So the Node runner reports 72 pass and 0 fail and exits 0 before any step runs, and the row does not show that the unit tests moved to `bun test`. A row that proves the change must check output that only `bun test` gives, for example its summary of 72 tests across 7 files, or the `test:unit` script text.
